rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-32: without the order, night operators (the class the curfew binds) would have opposed the residents' campaign for a curfew, which had run since 2023.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-1: without the order daytime movements would grow above 380 a day (about 3% a year) and off-peak runway capacity allows it.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-2: the WAA detects every movement from air traffic control's log and imposes penalties.

No matching assumption in WE-054; judged from the text: the log records every movement and the penalty is $10,000 per movement without a slot, so little daytime flying beyond the cap goes uncaught (A-14 concerns operators who are caught and pay in the curfew, not trade that escapes).

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-15: night operators, slot holders, would-be entrants and residents' associations can organize at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-3: holders expect slots to last past the 2032 review without reallocation.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-10: airlines differ in the value they get from a WXI slot.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-4: a slot market forms; slots are sold, leased and retimed at low transaction cost.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-054 (illustrative figures), A-5: airlines expected base-season history to set their share (the draft named the base seasons) and some could add off-peak daytime movements at a cost below the expected value of the extra slots.

Re-answered after the question was reworded to ask about the groups that gain from or are bound by the measure. No matching assumption in WE-054 for those groups; judged from the text: the residents' campaign has run since 2023, but the text does not say the airlines that now hold the night slots lobbied on night flying before; their stake, the slot rights, exists only under the order. (A-32 is about night operators opposing the campaign.)
